# Nuvero AI

> Nuvero AI (formerly Nexora AI) builds AI infrastructure: the intelligence layer a business runs on. Agents trained on how a company actually works, wired into the tools it already uses, running its manual workflows end to end. Every system is deployed in the client's own stack and the client owns all of the code.

Nuvero is led by founder and principal AI engineer Bhumit Goyal and works remotely from India with clients worldwide. Engagements are fixed-price and scoped per workflow; typical builds go from kickoff to production in 6 to 8 weeks, with weekly working demos.

Key facts:
- AI infrastructure, not a product subscription or hourly engagement: clients get a working systems layer they own outright (source code, runbooks, architecture docs).
- Deployed in the client's cloud accounts; no vendor lock-in; third-party API costs billed to the client at raw cost.
- 1.4M+ AI interactions handled per month across deployments; systems running across 11 industries.
- Security: encryption in transit and at rest, least-privilege access, DPA available; built with SOC 2 / GDPR / HIPAA considerations when relevant.
- Contact: contact@nuvero.space · https://www.nuvero.space/contact

- [Southwest Gases: Voice Concierge](https://www.nuvero.space/work/southwest-gases-voice-concierge) (Energy & Utilities): A natural-language voice agent that fields every customer call, navigates account-specific data, and runs outbound campaigns for the marketing team without ever sounding like a bot.

- [Meridian Realty: Inbound Qualifier](https://www.nuvero.space/work/meridian-realty-inbound-qualifier) (Real Estate): A voice + chat hybrid that responds to inbound property inquiries the moment they land, qualifies budget and timeline, and books site visits directly into agent calendars.
- [Multi-tenant: LinkedIn Lead Intelligence Engine](https://www.nuvero.space/work/linkedin-lead-intelligence-engine) (B2B SaaS & Agencies): A custom lead-gen system that scrapes targeted LinkedIn audiences, enriches via 6 data sources, cascades email verification across cheap APIs, and outputs personalized openers all in one script tailored per client.

## Briefings

- [The Infrastructure Readiness Report](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/infrastructure-readiness-report): A five-dimension rubric to grade how ready your business actually is to run AI in production, and where the layer breaks first.
- [Why your AI pilot never shipped](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/why-your-pilot-didnt-ship): The gap between a demo that works and a system that runs is not the model. It is the four things nobody scoped.
- [Own the layer](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/own-the-layer): Renting your intelligence by the seat is fine until it is the thing your business runs on. Then it is a liability.
- [Accuracy is the wrong metric](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/accuracy-is-the-wrong-metric): An agent that is right most of the time and unpredictable the rest of the time is not a good agent. It is an unmanaged one.
- [What to refuse first](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/what-to-refuse-first): Scoping a first AI system is mostly an exercise in saying no, and the things you refuse decide whether the thing you build ever ships.
- [Why retrieval projects stall](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/why-rag-stalls): Retrieval is not a vector database problem. It is a content problem, and most teams discover that after they have bought the database.
- [Where the handoff belongs](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/where-the-handoff-belongs): Human-in-the-loop is not a safety blanket you add at the end. It is a design decision that determines whether the system saves anyone any time.
- [The real cost of running agents](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/the-real-cost-of-agents): Token spend is the line item everyone models and the smallest one that matters. The costs that decide the business case sit somewhere else entirely.
- [Agents need least privilege more than people do](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/least-privilege-for-agents): You would not give a new hire admin credentials on their first day. Most agent deployments do exactly that, and call it an integration.
- [Start inside the building](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/start-inside-the-building): The highest-return first deployment is almost never the customer-facing one, and the reason has nothing to do with caution.
- [What trained on your business actually requires](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/trained-on-your-business): The phrase gets used to mean fine-tuning, and it almost never should. What most businesses need is context engineering, and it is a different budget.
- [Observability when the system is not deterministic](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/observability-for-non-deterministic-systems): Traditional monitoring asks whether the system responded. Agentic systems fail while responding perfectly, which is why most teams find out from a customer.
- [The latency budget is the product](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/the-latency-budget): Voice agents do not fail on comprehension. They fail on timing, and the budget is smaller than almost every architecture assumes.
- [Most multi-agent systems should be one agent](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/when-orchestration-is-overhead): Orchestration is presented as an architecture and is usually a workaround for a context problem that would be cheaper to solve directly.
- [Build, buy, or assemble](https://www.nuvero.space/briefings/build-buy-or-assemble): The build-versus-buy question is the wrong shape for the intelligence layer, because the real decision is which parts you can afford to have someone else own.
